title: HydrAMP generates antimicrobial peptide analogues validated in bacterial assays
summary: HydrAMP, a conditional variational autoencoder with antimicrobial activity classifiers, generated peptide analogues and de novo candidates. The 2022 preprint reports wet-lab confirmation of increased activity for a generated Pexiganan-based analogue; the 2023 journal version reports testing across five bacterial strains, including nine analogues of clinical prototypes and six analogues of an inactive peptide. The tested panel was small and model/human filtered; it does not establish therapeutic efficacy.
ai_technology: Conditional variational autoencoder with classifier-guided peptide generation and molecular-dynamics-based candidate preselection

evidence.tested: Generated peptide analogues were experimentally evaluated for antimicrobial activity across five bacterial strains; the journal abstract reports high activity for nine generated analogues of clinical prototypes and six analogues of an inactive peptide.
evidence.unknown: The tested panel is selected and small; these are in-vitro assays and do not establish safety, therapeutic efficacy or clinical benefit. The 2023 correction replaced a duplicated generation-statistics figure, not the wet-lab result stated here.
evidence.ai_role: A conditional VAE generated peptide analogues and unconstrained candidates from antimicrobial activity conditions; ranking and molecular-dynamics preselection helped choose candidates for experimental validation.

source_review.scope: Primary bioRxiv v1 abstract/metadata; primary Nature Communications indexed full article including methods/results; primary publisher author correction.
